clue.text: Continuous and repetitive sounds are monotonous

parts.note: a hum is a continuous low sound, with 'sounds' read for both halves
a drum gives out repeated beating sounds

explanation.surface: Droning, repeated noises are boring to listen to.
explanation.definitionFit: Something humdrum is dull and lacking variety, the same tedious sense as monotonous.

clue.text: Locust taking Kent harvest

definitions.meaning: an insect that jumps, like a grasshopper
a worker picking hops, a crop grown in the English county of Kent

explanation.definitionFit: A locust is a jumping insect; hops grown in Kent, south-east England, are gathered by pickers.

clue.text: This spike may damage the rails

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or damage
a railway line is the rails a train runs on

explanation.surface: A metal spike could wreck the railway track.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: a marlinespike is a sailor's spike, so 'This spike' is one named after the answer; 'may' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Marline is the thin cord worked with a pointed marlinespike, the tool named after it.

clue.text: Great fear of looking under the bed?

definitions.text: Great fear of looking under the bed?

parts.words: Great fear of looking under the bed?
parts.note: a child fears monsters beneath the bed; the political phrase is fear of communists lurking everywhere

explanation.walkthrough: 'Reds under the bed' was a Cold War phrase for alarm about hidden communists.
explanation.definitionFit: The Red Terror was the Bolshevik campaign of mass repression, also loosely a dread of communists.

clue.text: Riches held by young lady — are unlucky

definitions.note: here standing for unlucky events, a plural noun

indicators.note: held by means the riches sit inside the young lady

parts.note: miss is a title for a young unmarried woman
a fortune is great wealth

explanation.surface: A girl's wealth brings her bad luck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are' is a link; the definition reads as unlucky happenings.
explanation.definitionFit: Misfortunes are strokes of bad luck, mishaps that befall the unfortunate.

clue.text: Partners at a dance, say, return alone

parts.note: a gig is a live music event, of which a dance is one example

indicators.note: return tells us to turn the word for alone round so it reads backwards

parts.note: to go solo is to act alone

explanation.surface: Couples at a ball go back home on their own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns SOLO into OLOS, which follows GIG; 'at' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Gigolos were men hired as dancing companions, so paid escorts or partners.

clue.text: Idle talk of gravity as propellant

parts.note: g is the symbol for acceleration due to gravity

explanation.surface: Chatter about how gravity drives a rocket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'propellant' is a second definition, gas propelling aerosols, and 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Gas is chatter or empty talk, and also a gaseous propellant.

clue.text: Assess line-spacing

definitions.meaning: the distance between the two rails of a railway line

explanation.definitionFit: To gauge is to judge, and a railway's gauge is the width between its rails.

clue.text: Dizzy hero looking like hippie?

definitions.meaning: Dizzy was the nickname of the Victorian prime minister and novelist Disraeli; this is the hero of one of his novels
a hippie has plenty of hair, read as two words

explanation.definitionFit: Lothair is Disraeli's 1870 novel and its title character; split, it says much hair.

clue.text: Make away with your old secret

parts.note: to make away with something is to steal it
thy is the old form of your

explanation.surface: Steal off with what belonged to you long ago, quietly.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealthy means furtive or done covertly.

clue.text: For fun they imitate Port Said's characters

indicators.note: characters means the letters of the place name, here to be rearranged into a new word

explanation.surface: Comedians mimic the people of an Egyptian port city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' means letters: those of PORT SAIDS are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Parodists are satirists who mock others by comic imitation.

clue.text: Set free relative — she's no beginner

indicators.note: no beginner says the relative's opening letter is dropped

parts.note: an auntie is a relative

explanation.surface: An aunt, no novice, releases someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no beginner' drops the A from AUNTIE; 'she's' is a link, the aunt being female.
explanation.definitionFit: To untie a bound captive is to release them.

clue.text: The top class for typists?

definitions.meaning: the select upper group of society
a typewriter typeface of twelve characters to the inch

explanation.definitionFit: Elite means the best people, and is also the name of a typewriter type size.

clue.text: Cash down for varnish- used here?

definitions.meaning: varnish for fingers is painted on the hard tip of each finger

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means immediate payment, and read literally names where nail varnish goes.

clue.text: Give help to climbers with lozenges

definitions.text: Give help to climbers with lozenges

parts.words: Give help to climbers with lozenges
parts.note: climbers are plants, and lozenges are diamond shapes in the lattice that supports them

explanation.walkthrough: Climbers suggest mountaineers and lozenges throat sweets; both are plants and diamond shapes.
explanation.definitionFit: Trelliswork is a lattice of crossed strips, forming diamonds, used to support climbing plants.

clue.text: King has to play two parts

definitions.text: King has to play two parts

parts.words: King has to play two parts
parts.note: a monarch whose Shakespeare history play is in Part One and Part Two

explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare wrote the play about this king in two parts, so the king 'has two parts' to his play.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry IV of England is the title of a Shakespeare play in two parts.

clue.text: Banish a hundred-odd stories about that

indicators.note: about says the rearranged stories go round the other piece
odd means peculiar, so the word stories is rearranged

parts.note: A plus C, the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: Exile somebody for a hundred strange tales about them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' rearranges STORIES to OSTRISE, and 'about' puts it round AC; 'that' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To ostracise is to exclude someone from society, as Athenians exiled by vote.

clue.text: It's carried shoulder-high as part of religious investiture

definitions.text: It's carried shoulder-high as part of religious investiture

parts.words: It's carried shoulder-high as part of religious investiture
parts.note: a monastic garment worn hanging from the shoulders, given at a religious clothing ceremony

explanation.walkthrough: Shoulder-high suggests a triumphal procession; the scapula is the shoulder blade.
explanation.definitionFit: A scapular is a monk's sleeveless over-garment, or two cloth pieces worn over the shoulders.

clue.text: Document providing insurance for landlord?

parts.note: a policy covering you provides insurance
a landlord lets property, so is literally one who lets

explanation.surface: Paperwork setting out a property owner's insurance cover.
explanation.walkthrough: A landlord as 'letter' (one who lets) is the pun, flagged by the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A covering letter is the explanatory note sent with an enclosed document.

clue.text: Spicy, lively show no monotony!

definitions.meaning: a stage entertainment of mixed acts, the 'spice of life' of the proverb

explanation.definitionFit: Variety is a music-hall entertainment and also diversity, the proverbial spice of life.

clue.text: A recluse before taking the widow's offering

parts.note: ere is an old word for before
in the Gospels a poor widow gives two mites, tiny coins, to the temple

explanation.surface: A hermit who first accepted a widow's donation.
explanation.definitionFit: An eremite is a hermit, especially a Christian one living alone.

clue.text: Makes amends for what's broken by a stone

indicators.note: broken suggests something smashed, so the letters of a stone are reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone pays for a window smashed by a thrown rock.
explanation.definitionFit: To atone is to make reparation for a wrong.

clue.text: To make up for loss of acting power, Lisa prays

indicators.note: to make up means to put together anew, so the name and verb are reworked

explanation.surface: An actress who has lost her abilities turns to prayer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To make up' sounds theatrical but rearranges LISA PRAYS; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Paralysis is the loss of the ability to move or act.

clue.text: Disinfectant usually sold in container

indicators.note: the words act as a container, holding the answer within them

explanation.surface: A cleaning product generally sold in a bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: Lysol is a brand of cresol-based germicidal cleaner.

clue.text: Concerning article with ten parts

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: parts means separates and reassembles the number's letters

explanation.surface: About a piece of writing in ten sections.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parts' rearranges TEN to ENT after AN.
explanation.definitionFit: Anent is an old preposition meaning about or regarding.

clue.text: General with Scots regiment has a nasty look

parts.note: Robert E. Lee was the American Confederate general
RS stands for the Royal Scots, a British army regiment

explanation.surface: A commander with a Scottish unit wears an unpleasant expression.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Scots, abbreviated RS, was a famous regiment of the British Army.
explanation.definitionFit: To leer is to give a sly, lecherous or malicious glance.

clue.text: It's laid down in no amateur sense

parts.note: a pro, or professional, is no amateur
vision, or sight, is one of the senses

explanation.surface: A rule set out by an expert's eye.
explanation.definitionFit: A provision is a clause or condition stipulated in a law or contract.

clue.text: For which mercenaries defended what God abandoned (Housman)

definitions.text: For which mercenaries defended what God abandoned (Housman)

parts.words: For which mercenaries defended what God abandoned (Housman)
parts.note: Housman's poem on an army of mercenaries says they defended what God abandoned and saved the sum of things for money

explanation.walkthrough: The poem is A. E. Housman's Epitaph on an Army of Mercenaries.
explanation.definitionFit: Mercenaries fight for wages, the reward named in the poem's last line.

clue.text: Civil list beneficiary benefits author

definitions.meaning: the Civil List was the state's annual payment to Britain's monarch and family
a writer earns a fee on each copy sold

explanation.definitionFit: The royal family were paid from the Civil List, and a writer's percentage of sales is the same word.

clue.text: Rings of bird-watchers

definitions.meaning: guard rings worn to hold a more valuable ring on the finger
gamekeepers or zoo staff who guard and look after birds

explanation.definitionFit: Keeper rings guard other rings; keepers look after animals, birds included.
